# Source Notes

The source material has been distilled into this self-contained reference. Do not resolve the original local folders or source files.

## Bundled Knowledge Extract

- This skill is self-contained. Use the extract below as bundled pattern memory; do not resolve the original local folders or source documents.
- Start substantial BA artifacts with metadata: project/client, module or process, purpose, audience, source inputs, version/date, author/reviewer, and status.
- Separate confirmed facts, future-state requirements, business rules, assumptions, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and open questions.
- Use SRS-style coverage when scope is broad: business objectives, as-is/to-be, in-scope/out-of-scope, glossary, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, user requirements, functional requirements, NFRs, UI/reporting, external interfaces, and appendices.
- Keep requirements atomic, unambiguous, feasible, necessary, prioritized where useful, traceable to evidence, and testable through acceptance criteria or UAT evidence.
- Validate that each artifact can be understood independently by BA, Dev, QC, PM, Solution Architect, and client stakeholders without hidden source context.
- Verification checks whether the requirement is understandable, complete for the project phase, consistent with other requirements, feasible, modifiable, traceable, and free from vague terms.
- Validation checks whether the requirement supports a real stakeholder need, business objective, regulatory constraint, operational scenario, or measurable value outcome.
- Requirement analysis and design definition should specify/model requirements, verify requirements, validate requirements, define requirement architecture, define design options, and compare options by value, cost, risk, and feasibility.
- WBS/estimation support should break scope into capability, feature, workflow, screen, API/integration, data/report, migration, testing, release, and support components with assumptions and exclusions.
- Estimate inputs should surface complexity drivers such as unclear rules, third-party dependency, data volume/quality, non-standard UI, security constraints, performance needs, and testing breadth.

## Patterns Extracted

- Vision documents should cover purpose, document scope, references, business opportunity, problem statement, product position, stakeholders, user profiles, user environment, product overview, product features, priority, assumptions, dependencies, cost/pricing when applicable, and other requirements.
- Vision-level product features must be high-level capabilities with end-user benefits; detailed feature behavior belongs in use cases, SRS, or user stories.
- SRS overview structure emphasizes business objectives, as-is state, to-be state, scope, glossary, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, user requirements, functional requirements, NFRs, and appendices.
- Scope should explicitly separate in-scope and out-of-scope work.
- Existing-project reconstruction should distinguish source evidence from inferred statements.
